summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with relapsed multiple myeloma, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and CKD stage 3, was admitted with fevers and right eye swelling. Imaging confirmed right preseptal cellulitis and worsening sinus disease, and stool testing revealed C. difficile colitis. He was treated with IV antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral cephalexin, Bactrim, and vancomycin. His blood counts improved after two units of PRBCs, and his infection resolved. Chemotherapy was held during admission. He remained stable, with no complications, and was discharged home with a full course of oral antibiotics, instructions for hand hygiene, and follow-up plans with ENT and oncology.
